title: Reflexive 11: It Starts on Its Own (начинаться)
description: Many verbs have a -ся twin with no doer. Начинать урок (begin the lesson) versus Урок начинается (the lesson begins). The thing that was the object becomes the subject, and nobody is named as doing it.
descriptionRussian: У многих глаголов с прямым дополнением есть близнец на -ся без деятеля. «Начинать урок» и «Урок начинается». Бывший объект становится подлежащим, и никто не назван как тот, кто это делает.
intro: Close to the passive but not the same. These verbs come in twins: one where somebody does the thing, and one where the thing simply happens. Anton opens the door, and the door opens. English uses the same word for both and lets context sort it out. Russian marks the difference, and the mark is the ending you have been adding for ten lessons.
rules: Some verbs come in a pair: a plain verb with a doer and an object (Антон начинает урок) and a -ся twin with no doer (Урок начинается).
With the -ся twin, the word that was the object becomes the subject, and nobody is named as doing it: Дверь открывается (The door opens).
Choose the -ся twin when the thing happens on its own; choose the plain verb when you name a doer plus a separate thing being acted on.
The three pairs today: начинать / начинаться, открывать / открываться, закрывать / закрываться.
examples: Антон начинает урок. (Anton begins the lesson.) Plain verb: doer Антон, object урок.
Урок начинается в восемь. (The lesson begins at eight.) -ся twin: урок is the subject, no doer named.
Лена открывает магазин утром. (Lena opens the store in the morning.) Plain verb: doer Лена, object магазин.
Магазин открывается в девять. (The store opens at nine.) -ся twin: магазин is the subject, no doer named.
Сторож закрывает дверь. (The guard closes the door.) Plain verb: doer сторож, object дверь.
Дверь закрывается автоматически. (The door closes automatically.) -ся twin: дверь is the subject, no doer named.

tables.title: Plain verb (with doer) vs -ся twin (no doer)

items.promptEnglish: The lesson begins at eight o'clock.
items.hint: Is there a doer, or does the lesson start on its own?
items.explanation: Nobody is named as starting the lesson, so use the -ся twin: начинается. The subject is урок (singular), so the ending is -ется.

items.promptEnglish: The store opens at nine in the morning.
items.hint: No doer is named. The store opens on its schedule.
items.explanation: The store opens on its own schedule with no doer named, so the -ся twin открывается is right.

items.hint: The door acts on its own. Which form has no doer?
items.explanation: The door closes on its own ('automatically'), so use the -ся twin закрывается.

items.promptEnglish: Anton opens the door every morning.
items.hint: There is a doer (Антон) and a separate thing (дверь). Which form?
items.explanation: Here there is a doer (Антон) acting on a separate thing (дверь), so use the plain verb открывает.

items.promptEnglish: The concerts begin at exactly seven.
items.hint: The subject 'концерты' is plural. Is anyone named as starting them?
items.explanation: Nobody is named as starting the concerts, so use the -ся twin. The subject концерты is plural, so the ending is -ются: начинаются.

items.promptEnglish: Lena closes the store and goes home.
items.hint: Лена is the doer acting on the store. Plain verb or -ся twin?
items.explanation: Лена is the doer and магазин is the separate thing she acts on, so use the plain verb закрывает.

items.promptEnglish: The shops open at nine in the morning.
items.hint: No doer is named, and the subject is plural.
items.explanation: The shops open on their own schedule with no doer named, so the -ся twin, and the plural subject takes -ются: открываются.

items.hint: 'Автоматически' tells you no one is doing it.
items.explanation: The doors close by themselves, so the -ся verb; plural двери takes закрываются.

items.hint: The film is not ending anything - it ends by itself.
items.explanation: The film ends on its own, so the -ся verb: кончается.

blanks: Фильм _____ через пять минут. (The film begins in five minutes.)
Окна _____ автоматически вечером. (The windows close automatically in the evening.)
fillInBlank.grammarFocus: Both blanks need the -ся twin because no doer is named. Фильм is singular → начинается (-ется). Окна is plural → закрываются (-ются).

errorCorrection.translationEnglish: The film ends at ten o'clock.
errorCorrection.explanation: No doer is named, so use the -ся twin заканчивается: фильм is the subject and the film ends on its own. The plain verb заканчивает needs a doer plus an object (Учитель заканчивает урок), so it cannot stand alone here.

The concert goes on by itself with no doer named, so use the -ся twin продолжается. The plain verb продолжает needs a doer plus an object (Учитель продолжает урок), which leaves the sentence without a workable structure.

errorCorrection.translationEnglish: The doors close before the start of the film.
errorCorrection.explanation: Nobody is named as closing the doors, so use the -ся twin. The subject двери is plural, so the ending is -ются: закрываются. The plain verb закрывают ('they close [something]') names a doer plus needs a separate object.

minimalPairs.contextEnglish: Anton opens the store at eight in the morning.
minimalPairs.explanation: Антон is the doer and магазин is the separate thing he opens, so use the plain verb открывает. The -ся twin открывается would mean the store opens on its own with no doer, which contradicts naming Антон.

minimalPairs.contextEnglish: The store opens at eight in the morning.
minimalPairs.explanation: No doer is named; the store opens on its schedule, so use the -ся twin открывается. The plain verb открывает needs a doer plus an object (Антон открывает магазин).
'Сама' (by itself) shows there is no doer, so use the -ся twin закрывается. The plain verb закрывает would need a doer plus an object (Сторож закрывает дверь).

categorySorting.instruction: Sort each sentence: does it name a doer (use the plain verb) or does the thing act on its own (use the -ся twin)?

reviewVocab.definition: to begin, to start (the -ся twin of начинать; the thing begins on its own, with no doer named: Урок начинается)
reviewVocab.example: Концерт начинается ровно в семь часов вечера.

reviewVocab.definition: to open / to close (the -ся twins of открывать / закрывать; the thing opens or closes on its own, no doer named)
reviewVocab.example: Магазин открывается в девять и закрывается в десять.

reviewVocab.definition: to begin / open / close something (the plain verbs; each needs a doer plus a separate object: Антон открывает дверь)
reviewVocab.example: Лена открывает магазин утром, а Антон закрывает его вечером.
